Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity + autoscaling (next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard (high level):
- Primary workload: customer-facing conversational agent + follow-up reranking/embeddings pipeline for search relevance.
- Peak production traffic target: ~250 concurrent end-user sessions during peak, spiky distribution (burst ~1.5x for short windows).
- Avg sequence length: ~400 tokens (user + system + context); some long tails to ~1,200 tokens for troubleshooting flows.
- Embeddings: batch ingestion of documents (hourly) + realtime embedding for search/rerank on request path.
- Latency target: 95th %ile < 350ms for generation; embeddings < 150ms.

Open items / asks for sizing: 
1) Confirm expected peak RPS (requests/sec) for generation vs embeddings.
2) Typical batching window for embedding ingestion (do you batch hourly or near-real-time?).
3) Any hard constraints on concurrency per session (e.g., 1 request at a time vs pipelined requests).
4) Where will you host (VPC peering / AWS account vs on-prem)?

Next steps we propose: 
- I’ll kick off a short SRE/architecture deep-dive with our Solutions Engineering (Aditya) to validate autoscaling policy and queue sizing.
- Please fill in the attached sizing sheet (dedicated-sizing-model.xlsx) with any missing metrics — this helps us produce a preliminary capacity and cost estimate.
- Proposed meeting: Thu, Dec 3rd 10:00 AM PT for an SRE deep-dive (30–45m). Can you confirm?

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-model.xlsx (small template)

Thanks — I’ll bring our recommended autoscale ranges (min/max nodes), concurrency guardrails, and queue suggestions to the call.

Best,

Subject: Dedicated capacity notes: autoscaling, throughput, concurrency, queues, and auth (pre-SRE deep-dive)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks — reviewed the telemetry and the partially completed sizing sheet. A few technical notes to set expectations for the scheduled deep-dive: 

1) Autoscaling model (high level)
- We recommend a min/max node model for Dedicated: start with min=2 nodes (for redundancy) and max=12 nodes based on your burst profile — we'll refine after we see the completed sheet.
- Autoscale triggers: CPU/GPU utilization + request queue depth + P95 latency breaches. Use composite policies to avoid thrashing.
- Cooldown windows: 2–3 min scale-up; 10–15 min scale-down to avoid oscillation from short spikes.

2) Throughput sizing & concurrency
- For the model class you described (avg 400 tokens), estimate ~X tokens/sec per GPU depending on quantization and batch size — we’ll run more precise benching, but practically: aim for a soft concurrency cap per GPU and enforce per-session single concurrency.
- Recommended starting concurrency targets: 48 concurrent token-steps per GPU (translate to ~12–16 simultaneous short requests depending on batch profiles).

3) Queueing & burst handling
- Short bursts are best absorbed by a small request queue with a backpressure window. Suggest: per-node in-flight queue depth 1,000 requests (tunable) and a global admission controller with request timeouts set to your SLOs.
- Prefer token-aware batching inside the runtime + prefix KV cache to reduce repeated compute for conversational state.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Keep embedding ingestion off the low-latency path — dedicate background workers or separate pool if embeddings ingestion spikes could contend with generation.
- Reranking: consider a lightweight reranker model colocated with generation nodes if you need sub-200ms end-to-end; otherwise run as separate CPU workers and fetch scores asynchronously.

5) Auth & network (VPC peering)
- VPC peering + mTLS is a common pattern. For customer-managed KMS, we support integrating key wrapping for any stored secrets.
- For short-lived creds we recommend OAuth2-based service tokens rotated via your secret manager (we can provide a reference implementation).

6) Structured output & tool calling
- If you plan to use function/tool calling or structured JSON output, size for slightly higher latency per request (additional post-processing). We recommend enabling streaming responses and validating schema at the client side to fail fast.

7) Next steps for the deep-dive
- Please finalize the sizing sheet.
- Share a sample VPC CIDR and preferred peering window — we’ll provide network rules and a handshake checklist.
- We'll run a small bench (our side) against representative payloads once we have the final numbers.

I’ll bring an initial capacity plan and queueing policy to the Dec 3 call (assuming that time works).

Regards,
